clue.text: Wimp gets what he can out of work

parts.words: gets what he can out of
parts.note: to milk a person or situation is to extract every possible advantage
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A worker squeezes every last benefit from the job and is called a wimp for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A milksop is a feeble, spineless person, a synonym for a weakling or wimp.

clue.text: Mockingbird encompasses classy line with monkey flower

indicators.note: to encompass is to surround, so the bird goes round the other letters

parts.note: Mimus is the genus of the mockingbirds
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: A mockingbird surrounds a smart line of monkey flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U usages.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimulus is the botanical genus whose common name is monkey flower.

clue.text: Student making a bob or twenty?

parts.note: twenty shillings made a pound, abbreviated L from Latin libra
a bob was a shilling, so someone making one is an earner

explanation.surface: A student is asked whether they earn a shilling or perhaps twenty.
explanation.walkthrough: Old British money: a bob was a shilling, and twenty bob made a pound, written L (as in the £ sign).
explanation.definitionFit: A learner is someone studying a subject, a direct synonym for a student.

clue.text: Like this meat near Newmarket

parts.note: so means in this way
ham is cured pork

explanation.surface: Meat of this sort can be bought close to Newmarket.
explanation.walkthrough: Newmarket is an English horse-racing town; Soham is a small Cambridgeshire town nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Soham is a Cambridgeshire town a few miles from Newmarket, so it is a place lying near it.

clue.text: Game to leave with high pressure

parts.note: to part is to depart or leave
a ridge is a long area of high atmospheric pressure in weather maps

explanation.surface: Game birds take off as pressure rises.
explanation.definitionFit: The partridge is a game bird shot for sport and food.

clue.text: Obliterate reason for moue, do I ask?

indicators.note: the question form tells you to say the words aloud as a spoken query, so the result is a sound-alike

parts.note: a moue is a pout, so asking the reason for one is asking 'why pout?'

explanation.surface: Someone puzzled by a sulky face wonders what could explain it.
explanation.walkthrough: A moue is a pout, so the question 'why pout?', said aloud under 'do I ask', sounds like the phrase meaning destroy.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe out something is to destroy it completely, the same as obliterating it.

clue.text: Fail to pay dresser for rabbit?

definitions.meaning: to renege on a debt or bet
the word that comes before both dresser (a kitchen cupboard) and rabbit (cheese on toast)

explanation.surface: Someone skips paying for a cupboard to keep a pet rabbit in.
explanation.walkthrough: A Welsh dresser is a kitchen sideboard and Welsh rabbit (rarebit) is cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: To welsh on a debt is to fail to pay it, and the word also precedes both dresser and rabbit.

clue.text: Beer harvest coming up in in China

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means read from the bottom, so the run is reversed

parts.note: ale is beer
a crop is a harvest

explanation.surface: Beer and the harvest are rising in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns ALE + CROP into PORCELA; the first 'in' supplies IN and the second is a link. 'China' lost its capital in meaning here.
explanation.definitionFit: China is the everyday name for fine porcelain tableware, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Guzzle eggs, swallowing before tea, say

indicators.note: the eggs take in the next piece, as if gulping it down

parts.note: ova are eggs
ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: say signals that the following letter sounds like the drink

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like T

explanation.surface: Someone gobbles eggs, wolfing them down before tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guzzle' and 'eggs' read as one picture of greedy breakfast; ERE is an old poetic word for before.
explanation.definitionFit: To overeat is to eat too much, much the same as to guzzle.

clue.text: Opera gets the French in proportion

parts.note: Tosca is Puccini's opera
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An opera takes on a French article in proportion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something drawn to scale has every part in correct proportion to the original.

clue.text: Politician came out female

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of their usual order

parts.note: her is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A politician has publicly come out as a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges CAME into MEAC. Michael Meacher was a long-serving Labour MP and minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Meacher was a British Labour politician, so his surname answers a clue for a politician by example.

clue.text: Bounty's lost leader's gear dispersed on ship

definitions.note: read as 'bounty is', the definition plus a link

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter
scattered, so the letters of gear are spread into a new order

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: The Bounty has lost its captain and its equipment is strewn about the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispersed' makes ARGE from GEAR. The surface recalls HMS Bounty, whose captain Bligh was cast adrift.
explanation.definitionFit: Largess is generous giving, a synonym for bounty in the sense of liberal gifts.

clue.text: Fool's day delayed event in China?

definitions.meaning: April Fools' Day falls on the first of April; if the month before ran on, the day would come late
the 1934-35 retreat of the Chinese Communist army led by Mao

explanation.surface: April Fools' Day has been postponed by some happening in China.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is whimsical: a third month that went on too long would push back the first of April.
explanation.definitionFit: The Long March was the historic retreat of Mao's Red Army across China in 1934-35.

clue.text: Clearing out medicine for hygiene, maybe

indicators.note: the letters stand for, or are carried within, the following words

explanation.surface: A purgative is recommended as a hygiene measure.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across the junction of 'hygiene' and 'maybe'; 'for' is a loose pointer to letters carried inside those words.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema is a liquid injected to flush out the bowel, a medicine used for clearing it out.

clue.text: Pole on cliff to end in stew

parts.note: S is the south pole
a crag is a steep rugged rock face

explanation.surface: A pole perched on a cliff edge seems doomed to finish up in a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a fill-in: scrag end, the bony neck of mutton, is the cut that goes into a stew.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrag is the neck of mutton; the phrase scrag end names the cheap cut used for stewing.

clue.text: Curt and inelegant way to control motorists

definitions.text: Curt and inelegant way to control motorists

indicators.note: read inelegant way as the letters of inelegant set out another way

explanation.surface: A brusque, graceless instruction is a way of keeping drivers in order.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a terse road order; 'way' asks for the letters of INELEGANT in a new way, and 'Curt and' describes the command's tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Get in lane is a terse traffic instruction ordering drivers into the right lane.

clue.text: Take apart that famous wedding dress?

parts.note: Di's, as in the 1981 wedding of Diana, Princess of Wales
a mantle is a cloak or garment

explanation.surface: The question asks whether this is the celebrated royal bridal gown.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Diana, known as Di, married Prince Charles in 1981 in a famous ivory gown.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle something is to take it to pieces, a direct synonym for taking apart.

clue.text: Concession opening shortly is likely to send one off

parts.note: a sop is a small concession to appease someone

indicators.note: cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: an orifice is an opening

explanation.surface: A concession made briefly at an opening seems likely to see one dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' clips ORIFICE to ORIFIC. 'send one off' suggests a red card but means send to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Soporific means tending to induce sleep, so it sends one off to sleep.

clue.text: A new plate for entering good prize at event in China

indicators.note: one piece goes into another, so the scrambled letters are placed inside the prize

parts.note: a reward is a prize

indicators.note: made new, so the letters of a, plate and for are given a fresh order

explanation.surface: A new plate is being entered for a good prize at some Chinese competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' makes ATLEAP from A PLATE; FOR stays as written. 'at' is only a link, and 'event in China' looks like part of the surface but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Leap Forward was Mao's disastrous 1958-62 campaign to industrialise China rapidly.

clue.text: Jolly good publicity for the …

parts.note: grand means splendid
an ad is an advertisement

explanation.surface: Excellent publicity aimed at older people, continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on into 18 down, whose answer completes the definition: a grandad is one of the elderly.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandad is a grandfather, typically an older man, so he belongs among the elderly.

clue.text: … shrub with tips from laboratory getting on

parts.note: the elder is a shrub bearing elderflowers and berries

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A shrub is being given tips by a laboratory.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on is an idiom for growing old, so it means advanced in years.

clue.text: Magnate died after kidnap

indicators.note: after places the piece for died behind the piece for kidnap

parts.note: to nab is to seize or snatch
OB is short for Latin obiit, he or she died

explanation.surface: A tycoon was killed after being abducted.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob is a very rich, powerful person, originally one who made a fortune in India.

clue.text: Guns against water, not including storm

parts.note: bar means except, as in all bar one
to rage is to storm

explanation.surface: Artillery is turned against floodwater except when it is stormy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against water' is a second hint: a barrage is also a dam built across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrage is a concentrated burst of artillery fire from many guns.

clue.text: Little boy bisects insects as well

indicators.note: to bisect is to cut in two, so the boy splits the insects

parts.note: bees are insects
Sid is a short form of Sidney

explanation.surface: A small boy cuts insects in half, along with other things.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides means also or in addition, the same as as well.

clue.text: Celtic saint put name to work of …

parts.note: the work of the composer named in the next clue, Verdi, whose opera is Aida

explanation.surface: Someone attaches a name to a piece by a composer, continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into 23 across, whose composer is Verdi; Aida is his opera. 'put ... to' just joins N to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Aidan was the Irish monk who founded the monastery at Lindisfarne, a Celtic saint.

clue.text: … composer with old grey copper's coat

parts.note: Giuseppe Verdi, the Italian opera composer
gris is an obsolete English word for grey, borrowed from French

explanation.surface: A composer is pictured alongside an elderly copper wearing a grey coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman in the surface, but here it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdigris is the green patina that forms on copper or brass, the metal's coating.

clue.text: It's a must to be opposed to a lot of Europeans

parts.note: V is versus, against

indicators.note: most of a word, so the end is dropped

parts.note: Italians are Europeans

explanation.surface: It is essential to stand against a great many Europeans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' cuts ITALIANS to ITAL; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vital is essential, so it is a must.

clue.text: Where is Rangers' team holding world up?

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, reversing the whole
the team holds the world inside it

parts.note: XI is a team of eleven, as in football or cricket
an orb is a globe or world

explanation.surface: Someone asks where the Rangers side is that is delaying the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the lot, as the clue is a down light. Ibrox is the Glasgow stadium of Rangers football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibrox Stadium in Glasgow is the home ground of Rangers, so it is where Rangers play.

clue.text: Jolly worker after party having a kip

indicators.note: after places the jolly worker behind the party

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
a Jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
a worker ant is the stock crossword worker

explanation.surface: A cheerful labourer dozes off after a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like an adjective but is old naval slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormant means inactive as if asleep, so it fits someone having a kip, British slang for a nap.

clue.text: See 17
Isn't alcohol permitted to one imprisoned for battery?

parts.note: a dry place or event is one where alcohol is banned
a cell is home to anyone imprisoned

explanation.surface: A prisoner asks whether drink is banned for him, and why he is facing a battery charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry cell is a type of electric battery using paste instead of liquid electrolyte.

clue.text: Apples keep student on top of studies with no one else to steer

definitions.text: with no one else to steer

indicators.note: to keep is to hold, so the apples hold the student inside

parts.note: Coxes are Cox's Orange Pippin apples
L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates

indicators.note: the top of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Apples keep a pupil going while studying with no one around to guide him.
explanation.walkthrough: Cox's Orange Pippin is a popular British apple. Coxless describes a rowing boat without a cox to steer it.
explanation.definitionFit: A coxless boat has no coxswain, so the rowers steer it themselves.
